title: Survival Kit
tagline: When you don't understand, when you're lost, when you need help.
canDo: You can rescue a conversation and handle an emergency in Urdu

grammar.title: aana: knowing a language
grammar.body: Skills 'come to you': mujhe Urdu aati hai (I know Urdu), kya aapko angrezi aati hai? (do you speak English?). The verb agrees with the language (feminine: aati).

grammar.title: ko bulaiye, se allergy, ke paas
grammar.body: doctor ko bulaiye (call a doctor). moongphali se allergy (allergic to peanuts). mere paas paise nahin hain (I have no money): 'paas' (near) is how Urdu says 'have' for things you carry.

grammar.title: Who is speaking: -a or -i
grammar.body: A man says gaya hoon, raha hoon, sakta hoon. A woman says gayi hoon, rahi hoon, sakti hoon. The rest of the sentence stays the same.

lessons.title: Say that again?
lessons.blurb: The four phrases that rescue every conversation.
lessons.canDo: You can stop a conversation that's going too fast and get it repeated

teach.title: You're allowed to not understand
teach.info: Fluent speakers do this all day. Saying 'dobara kahiye' in Urdu keeps the conversation in Urdu. Switching to English ends it.

teach.tip: Many people say 'aaya' instead of 'aayi'. Both are understood.
zara = 'a bit'. It softens any request.

exercises.question: What does Ammi ask Pervez to do?

options.feedback: No price yet. He hasn't even started the meter.

exercises.setup: Outside the airport. Pervez talks the way he drives.

exercises.prompt: The shopkeeper said a price and you missed it.

exercises.explain: jaldi means quickly. That's the opposite of what you need.

lessons.title: What's this called?
lessons.blurb: Turn every person you meet into a free Urdu teacher.
lessons.canDo: You can ask what a thing is called and what a word means

teach.tip: Point at anything and say this. People love being asked.
aana (to come) is how Urdu says you know a language: it 'comes to you'.
Last resort. But now you can ask it in Urdu.

exercises.prompt: You're holding a vegetable you've never seen before.

exercises.explain: Urdu (the language) is feminine, so it's aati hai.

lessons.title: Help!
lessons.blurb: Hopefully never needed. Learn it anyway.
lessons.canDo: You can call for help and say who you need

teach.tip: mujhe … jana hai: I need to go to …

options.text: In her bag the whole time

options.feedback: That's what she thought. Listen to her last line.
Abbu offered to call them. He didn't need to.

lessons.title: Lost and broke
lessons.blurb: No phone, no wallet, no idea where you are. A normal Tuesday in Anarkali.
lessons.canDo: You can explain that you're lost or that something's been lost or stolen

teach.title: gaya or gayi?
teach.info: The verb ending shows who is speaking: a man says bhool gaya hoon and kar sakta hoon, a woman says bhool gayi hoon and kar sakti hoon. Things have gender too: phone kho gaya (masculine), ghari kho gayi (feminine).

teach.tip: mere paas = 'near me'. It's how Urdu says 'I have'.

exercises.explain: -a endings for a man, -i endings for a woman.

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.blurb: Say what's wrong, say what you need, say what you can't eat.
lessons.canDo: You can say you're unwell, ask for medicine and mention an allergy

teach.tip: tabiyat = how you're feeling in general. It covers everything from a cold to regret.
X se allergy: allergic 'from' X. Swap in doodh (milk), anda (egg), dhool (dust).

exercises.question: What does Bilal tell Nani to do?

options.feedback: He's a doctor. He never misses a chance to prescribe at home.

exercises.explain: chahiye always takes mujhe ('to me'), never main.

exercises.prompt: Someone apologises for bumping into you.

lessons.title: Mix it up
lessons.blurb: Your phone is at 4%. Warm up for the boss.
lessons.canDo: You can use this unit's phrases without a prompt: you can rescue a conversation and handle an emergency in Urdu

teach.title: Your phone is at 4%
teach.info: You're somewhere in Lahore, the driver has gone, and nobody around you speaks English. Run through the kit.

Nani is waiting. Say: “I need to go to the hospital”
Type it for the family group: “Can I make a phone call?”

boss.title: Lost in Anarkali
boss.blurb: Phone dead, driver gone, and Bashir Bhai gives directions at full speed.
boss.scene: Anarkali bazaar, late afternoon. You stepped out of the car to look at one thing. That was forty minutes ago. A shopkeeper waves you in.
boss.canDo: You can get yourself out of trouble in Urdu: explain the problem, slow people down, ask for what you need

options.reaction: He grins. Foreign-returned, trying in Urdu: his favourite kind of customer.

f.prompt: You need to reach your family.

h.prompt: He's handing you his phone and a cup of chai.

end.title: You got yourself found
end.text: You explained the problem, slowed him down, and borrowed a phone, all in Urdu. Ammi is on her way. Bashir Bhai is on his second cup and is now telling you about his nephew in Manchester.

story.title: The missing phone
story.blurb: Liberty Market. Your phone is gone. Or is it?

options.feedback: Ghayab, but only from your attention.
Meri jeb mein: in my pocket.

questions.question: What did you ask Bashir Bhai?

options.feedback: Not this time: aap ka phone istemal kar sakta hoon?
You asked to use his phone.
